templates.question: What is the shape, location, spread, and possible multimodality of a continuous measurement?

requiredStatistics.name: histogram bin boundaries and kernel density estimate
assumptions: Bin policy is declared before rendering.
Density bandwidth and boundary handling are recorded.

templates.question: At each threshold, what proportion of observations lies at or below it?

requiredStatistics.name: empirical cumulative probability
assumptions: Ties use a declared right-continuous step convention.
Observation weights are absent or explicitly normalized.

templates.question: How do complete group distributions differ while retaining medians, quartiles, and individual observations?

requiredStatistics.name: group quartiles and kernel density
assumptions: Group sample sizes are reported.
Jitter is deterministic and does not encode a measured dimension.

templates.question: How does a continuous distribution shift across ordered conditions or repeated epochs?

requiredStatistics.name: condition-specific kernel densities
assumptions: A common scale and declared bandwidth policy are used.
Each condition has enough observations for density estimation.

templates.question: Where and how strongly does an observed distribution depart from a declared reference distribution?

requiredStatistics.name: ordered sample and reference quantiles
assumptions: The reference family and fitted parameters are declared.
Pointwise or simultaneous envelopes are identified when present.

templates.question: How do ordered observations depart from the quantiles of each explicitly fitted probability family?

requiredStatistics.name: maximum-likelihood candidate quantiles
assumptions: Every fitted family and parameterization is declared.
Plotting positions and support restrictions are fixed before rendering.

templates.question: Across the cumulative range, where does each explicitly fitted probability family diverge from the empirical distribution?

requiredStatistics.name: maximum-likelihood fitted cumulative probability
assumptions: The empirical plotting-position convention is declared.
Goodness-of-fit inference is not inferred from visual proximity alone.

templates.question: What are the study or subgroup effect estimates, their uncertainty, and their relative precision?

requiredStatistics.name: verified point estimates and confidence bounds
assumptions: Every interval level and effect scale are identical or visibly stratified.
Null value and transformation are declared.

templates.question: Which model coefficients are directionally and practically important after uncertainty is shown?

requiredStatistics.name: model coefficient estimates and confidence intervals
assumptions: Covariance estimator and interval level are recorded.
Reference levels and coefficient scale are visible.

templates.question: How do group means or marginal means differ once uncertainty and sample support are visible?

requiredStatistics.name: group or marginal mean intervals
assumptions: Adjustment set and estimand are declared.
Intervals use the same covariance and multiplicity policy.

templates.question: How do condition mean ranks vary across the ordered repeated conditions in a complete blocked design?

requiredStatistics.name: Friedman condition rank sums and mean ranks
assumptions: Every included block has one complete observation for every ordered condition.
Tied values use deterministic average ranks within each block and the omnibus test declares its tie correction.

templates.question: How stable is an estimator across the declared resampling procedure, and where does the observed estimate lie?

requiredStatistics.name: bootstrap interval and observed estimator
assumptions: Resampling unit, replicate count, and random seed are recorded.
Interval construction method is declared.

templates.question: Do two measurement methods agree across their range, and are differences practically acceptable?

requiredStatistics.name: mean paired difference and limits of agreement
assumptions: Pairs are correctly matched.
Difference behavior and repeated-measure structure are reviewed.

templates.question: Do residual location, spread, or nonlinear structure change across fitted values?

requiredStatistics.name: residual smoother and zero reference
assumptions: Residual definition matches the fitted model family.
Smoother settings are fixed and recorded.

templates.question: Are model residual tails and central quantiles compatible with the declared reference distribution?

requiredStatistics.name: residual and reference quantiles
assumptions: Residual standardization and reference family are declared.
Envelope type is labeled when present.

templates.question: Is residual variance approximately constant over the fitted response range?

requiredStatistics.name: square-root absolute standardized residual and smoother
assumptions: Standardization uses the declared model covariance.
The smoother is descriptive rather than a formal variance test.

templates.question: Which observations combine unusual predictor leverage with influential residual behavior?

requiredStatistics.name: Cook distance contours and leverage thresholds
assumptions: Influence definition matches the fitted model.
Thresholds are screening aids rather than automatic exclusions.

templates.question: How closely do fitted predictions track observed outcomes over the full response range?

requiredStatistics.name: identity reference and prediction-error summary
assumptions: Training and evaluation partitions are explicitly labeled.
Prediction metrics use the same outcome scale as the plot.

templates.question: How does sensitivity trade against false-positive rate across all decision thresholds?

requiredStatistics.name: threshold-specific sensitivity, specificity, and area under curve
assumptions: Positive class and score direction are declared.
Evaluation observations are independent at the resampling unit.

templates.question: How does precision trade against recall under the observed class prevalence?

requiredStatistics.name: threshold-specific precision, recall, and average precision
assumptions: Positive class and prevalence are reported.
Ties use a deterministic threshold convention.

templates.question: Which observed classes are confused with which predicted classes at a declared threshold or decision rule?

requiredStatistics.name: class-pair counts and declared normalization
assumptions: Class order is fixed.
Raw counts remain available when row or column proportions are shown.

templates.question: Do predicted probabilities agree with observed event frequencies across the score range?

requiredStatistics.name: binned or smoothed observed event rate with uncertainty
assumptions: Binning or smoothing policy is declared.
Evaluation data are distinct from model fitting or clearly labeled.

templates.question: Which operating threshold balances the pre-specified error costs and performance metrics?

requiredStatistics.name: threshold-indexed sensitivity, specificity, precision, and utility
assumptions: Metric definitions and decision costs are pre-specified.
Threshold selection and performance estimation use separated data when claimed confirmatory.

templates.question: How does event-free survival change over time within each group under right censoring?

requiredStatistics.name: Kaplan-Meier survival estimate and pointwise interval
assumptions: Censoring convention and time origin are declared.
Independent censoring is a substantive assumption, not inferred from the curve.

templates.question: What is the cumulative probability of each competing event type over time?

requiredStatistics.name: cause-specific cumulative incidence and interval
assumptions: Competing outcomes and censoring codes are mutually exclusive and declared.
The estimator does not treat competing events as ordinary censoring.

templates.question: Which covariates or subgroups have materially different relative hazards after uncertainty is shown?

requiredStatistics.name: hazard ratios and confidence intervals
assumptions: Model adjustment set, tie method, and interval covariance are declared.
Proportional-hazards diagnostics are reported separately.

templates.question: Are group survival curves approximately parallel on the complementary log-log scale?

requiredStatistics.name: complementary log-log survival transform
assumptions: Undefined terminal probabilities are excluded by a declared rule.
Visual parallelism is a diagnostic screen, not a formal proof.

templates.question: How many participants remain at risk, experience events, or are censored at clinically meaningful times?

requiredStatistics.name: at-risk, event, and censoring counts by landmark
assumptions: Landmark times are fixed before tabulation.
Entry and censoring conventions match the accompanying survival curve.

templates.question: Which variable pairs have strong positive or negative association, and where are clusters of association visible?

requiredStatistics.name: pairwise association matrix and sample counts
assumptions: Association measure and missing-data policy are declared.
Multiplicity and dependence are not hidden by color saturation.

templates.question: How are observations separated in component space, and which variables drive that separation?

requiredStatistics.name: component scores, loadings, and explained variance
assumptions: Centering, scaling, retention, and deterministic sign conventions are recorded.
Scores and loading arrows use a declared biplot scaling.

templates.question: Which observations and variables form stable blocks of similar multivariate profiles?

requiredStatistics.name: scaled matrix and hierarchical clustering order
assumptions: Distance, linkage, scaling, and missing-data policies are declared.
Clustering is descriptive unless stability has been separately quantified.

templates.question: Which multivariate profiles, tradeoffs, and outlying combinations recur across observations?

requiredStatistics.name: declared per-axis normalization
assumptions: Axis order and scaling are fixed and visible.
Overplotting controls do not suppress observations.

templates.question: Are pairwise relationships linear, nonlinear, grouped, or driven by a small number of observations?

requiredStatistics.name: pairwise smoothers and marginal distributions
assumptions: All panels use consistent missing-data and scaling policies.
Smoothers are labeled descriptive unless specified by the analysis plan.

templates.question: How does a measured series evolve over time, including uncertainty, gaps, and interventions?

requiredStatistics.name: time-indexed estimate and uncertainty band
assumptions: Sampling cadence, aggregation, and missing-time policies are declared.
Uncertainty bands identify whether they represent measurement, sampling, or prediction uncertainty.

templates.question: At which lags does serial dependence remain after the declared transformation or model?

requiredStatistics.name: sample autocorrelation, partial autocorrelation, and reference bounds
assumptions: Regular spacing and differencing policy are declared.
Reference bounds are labeled approximate and use the effective sample size.

templates.question: Which frequencies account for dominant periodic variation in the measured signal?

requiredStatistics.name: windowed spectral density estimate
assumptions: Sampling interval, detrending, window, overlap, and scaling are recorded.
Aliasing and frequency resolution limits are reported.

templates.question: When do transient frequency components emerge, disappear, or change amplitude?

requiredStatistics.name: time-frequency power matrix
assumptions: Transform family, scales, padding, and cone-of-influence treatment are recorded.
Color scale represents power on a declared linear or logarithmic scale.

templates.question: What is the average signal response before and after a repeated event, and how variable is that response?

requiredStatistics.name: event-aligned mean and uncertainty band
assumptions: Alignment event, baseline correction, and within-event dependence are declared.
Uncertainty respects the event or subject resampling unit.

templates.question: Which combinations of categorical levels account for the largest departures from independence?

requiredStatistics.name: cell counts, expected counts, and standardized residuals
assumptions: Sampling design and structural zeros are declared.
Area encodes observed frequency and color uses a symmetric residual scale.

templates.question: Which row and column categories share similar association profiles in a contingency table?

requiredStatistics.name: correspondence coordinates, masses, and explained inertia
assumptions: Input counts and structural zeros are verified.
Coordinate normalization and retained dimensions are declared.

templates.question: How do binary associations vary across strata once uncertainty and sparse support are shown?

requiredStatistics.name: verified odds ratios and confidence bounds
assumptions: Continuity corrections and interval method are declared.
Sparse or zero cells remain visible in support annotations.

templates.question: Which contingency-table cells contribute most strongly to the omnibus association?

requiredStatistics.name: observed counts, expected counts, and standardized residuals
assumptions: Expected-count adequacy and structural zeros are reviewed.
Residual scale and multiplicity policy are stated.

templates.question: How do categorical compositions flow across ordered stages without losing the underlying counts?

requiredStatistics.name: stage-to-stage transition counts and proportions
assumptions: Stages have a fixed order and units are consistently linked.
Ribbon widths preserve absolute or proportional counts under a declared policy.

templates.question: How does a fitted response change jointly over two quantitative predictors inside the exact observed support domain?

requiredStatistics.name: model prediction surface and observed-domain mask
assumptions: The fitted model, fixed covariates, and prediction scale are declared.
Extrapolated regions are masked rather than presented as observed support.

templates.question: What clusters, gradients, and outlying observations remain visible across orthogonal projections of three measured dimensions?

requiredStatistics.name: axis ranges and robust coordinate summaries
assumptions: Axis units and transformations are declared.
Occlusion is mitigated without dropping observations.

templates.question: Where are high or low scalar values located across declared orthogonal slices of a three-dimensional sampled volume?

requiredStatistics.name: volume intensity domain and slice coordinates
assumptions: Voxel spacing, orientation, and units are recorded.
Clipping and transfer-function limits remain visible.

templates.question: How do vector direction and magnitude vary across orthogonal projections of a sampled three-dimensional domain?

requiredStatistics.name: vector magnitude and declared sampling mask
assumptions: Coordinate frame, component units, and vector scaling are recorded.
Subsampling is deterministic and preserves extrema.

templates.question: How does a measured object or state move through three-dimensional numeric space across synchronized orthogonal projections?

requiredStatistics.name: ordered path length, displacement, and time encoding
assumptions: Coordinate frame and temporal sampling are declared.
Interpolation is disabled or explicitly identified.

templates.question: How do individual study estimates, uncertainty intervals, inverse-variance weights, and fixed or random pooled effects compare on one declared scale?

requiredStatistics.name: verified study intervals and declared fixed or random inverse-variance pooled summaries
assumptions: All effects use a common declared scale and direction.
Within-study variances and the between-study variance estimator are recorded.

templates.question: Is the relation between study effect and standard error visually asymmetric around the declared pooled estimate and normal pseudo-limits?

requiredStatistics.name: declared pooled center and normal pseudo-limits
assumptions: The display is treated as an asymmetry screen rather than a publication-bias verdict.
Effect-scale behavior and heterogeneity are reviewed before interpretation.

templates.question: How much do the pooled effect and between-study variance change when each study is omitted exactly once?

requiredStatistics.name: complete leave-one-out fixed and random-effects recomputation
assumptions: Every row omits exactly one identified study from the same input set.
Influence is interpreted as sensitivity and does not authorize exclusion.

templates.question: Where are paired observations concentrated across the declared two-dimensional numeric bin grid?

requiredStatistics.name: complete deterministic two-dimensional bin counts
assumptions: The numeric x and y bin boundaries are declared and non-overlapping.
The color scale encodes counts and is not interpreted as a correlation coefficient.

templates.question: Do balanced factorial cell means change non-additively across the levels of the two declared fixed factors?

requiredStatistics.name: balanced complete-factorial cell means and standard errors
assumptions: The displayed cells come from the same balanced fixed-effects ANOVA fit.
Line crossing or separation is interpreted with the formal interaction test and design assumptions.

templates.question: How are observed counts distributed across the exact row-by-column contingency table while expected counts remain inspectable?

requiredStatistics.name: complete observed contingency counts with optional expected counts and residuals
assumptions: Every table cell is represented exactly once.
Color encodes observed count and must not be described as standardized-residual intensity.

templates.question: How does each declared multiple-testing correction transform every raw p value on the common probability scale?

requiredStatistics.name: exact declared-family multiple-testing correction
assumptions: The hypothesis family and correction method are declared before interpretation.
The display does not add a significance threshold or selection decision that is absent from the source.

templates.question: How much variance does each principal component explain, and how quickly does retained cumulative variance increase?

requiredStatistics.name: ordered eigendecomposition variance proportions
assumptions: The covariance or correlation scaling choice is recorded.
Component retention is displayed as a researcher decision rather than inferred from the chart.

templates.question: How are exact observation scores distributed across the first retained principal components without implying loading vectors?

requiredStatistics.name: exact retained principal-component scores
assumptions: Every input row is preserved without sampling or aggregation.
Axes report explained-variance context and no loading-vector biplot is claimed.

templates.question: Which variables contribute positively or negatively to each principal component on the declared loading scale?

requiredStatistics.name: signed principal-component loadings
assumptions: The covariance or correlation scaling choice is recorded.
A zero-centered diverging scale is used and deterministic eigenvector signs are disclosed.

templates.question: How does the complete evenly spaced observed series evolve relative to its fitted deterministic linear trend?

requiredStatistics.name: complete observation rows and deterministic linear trend
assumptions: Sampling is evenly spaced and every analyzed row is preserved.
The fitted trend is not presented as a forecast or stationarity model.

templates.question: At which lags does the sample autocorrelation exceed the declared approximate white-noise screening bounds?

requiredStatistics.name: sample autocorrelation and approximate white-noise bounds
assumptions: The analyzed transformation and maximum lag are declared.
Bounds are treated as screening guides rather than a stationarity decision or fitted-model interval.

templates.question: How does the population-level fixed-effect prediction change across one declared numeric or categorical predictor while other fixed terms remain at declared reference values?

requiredStatistics.name: fixed-effect marginal prediction and pointwise model-based confidence interval
assumptions: The profiled predictor and every held fixed value are recorded in the analysis artifact.
The profile stays inside observed predictor support and is not presented as subject-specific prediction.

templates.question: How do exact within-group observations and conditional fitted values differ across the declared observation order without inventing an undeclared time axis?

requiredStatistics.name: exact source-order observations and random-intercept conditional fitted values
assumptions: Every included observation is preserved without sampling or aggregation.
Within-group row order is labelled as order rather than time unless time is explicitly bound.

templates.question: Which groups have positive or negative conditional random-intercept estimates after shrinkage, and how uncertain is each plug-in estimate?

requiredStatistics.name: empirical-Bayes random-intercept BLUP and plug-in conditional uncertainty
assumptions: The intervals condition on fitted variance parameters and are not simultaneous group tests.
Extreme estimates trigger source-data review and do not authorize automatic exclusion.

templates.question: Do conditional residuals or random-intercept estimates show variance patterns or quantile departures that require model review before scientific interpretation?

requiredStatistics.name: conditional residual-versus-fitted screen and deterministic residual and random-intercept normal quantiles
assumptions: Every diagnostic panel identifies whether rows or groups are being assessed.
Q-Q alignment is a descriptive model check and does not validate Gaussian assumptions by itself.
